claim: A full audit refuses one test file on most runs, and a different file each run, so the tests-pass verdict an audit writes is not reproducible. Six audits on 2026-09-19 wrote six verdicts, five of them refusing exactly one of the 1,764 test files, and no two named the same file. A gate that refuses a file drawn at random is a gate nobody can act on: whoever reads the refusal mends a file that was never broken, and the file that is broken goes on being refused nowhere. It predates the concurrent runner, so concurrency is not its cause, but whether concurrency raised its rate is open.

evidence:
Read on 2026-09-19 out of tests-pass.check-code.audit.logs.uncommitted.jsonl, which holds one verdict row a round with the commit and the refusals.

The rows, oldest first. At 438edc9c4d63 and four commits carried with it, on the runner that ran one test file at a time, one refusal, agent/messaging/modules/message-file/message-file.module.test.ts. At 13fcc82d2cb2, twice, on that same runner, clean. At 55d921791f82, twice, on that same runner, one refusal, check/modules/audit-listening/audit-listening.module.test.ts. At abfa951094e1, with test files running several at a time, one refusal, code/ios-harness/scripts/render-harness-run/render-harness-run.shell-script.scripting.test.ts. At d4bded126676, with checks running several at a time too, one refusal, agent/model/gateway/modules/gateway-tree-version/gateway-tree-version.module.test.ts. At 79741ad8153e and aa5115a3377e, one refusal, alan/web/modules/alan-auth-provider/alan-auth-provider.module.test.tsx.

So two of four rounds on the serial runner were clean and none of three rounds on the concurrent runner was. That is too few rounds to tell a rate from, and it is the only reason to suspect concurrency at all. The two serial rounds that refused sit either side of the change, so the shape is older than the change.

The newest refusal is the one that shows the fault is not in the file blamed. The run said `SyntaxError: Export named 'postDeviceToken' not found in module '/var/tmp/akasha-overlay-rgHC78/lane4/merged/alan/web/modules/push-registration-sync/push-registration-sync.module.code.tsx'`. That module states `export async function postDeviceToken` on its own line, and alan-auth-provider.module.test.tsx does not import it at all, naming only bun:test, @testing-library/react, use-use-user-id and react. So the runner read a module it could not resolve an export from, in a file the test reaches only through something it mocks, and the export is there in the tree the overlay was built from.

What that round did otherwise: 19,007 tests over 1,764 test files, one failing, and 56 checks with none unmeasured. So the failure is one file in eighteen hundred rather than a broad breakage, and no check was killed or left unrun.

What is not established: whether a file named once is named again at the same commit, since a verdict fresh at a commit is carried rather than run and a second round writes no second run. Nothing here ran one of those files alone to see it refuse on its own, and until one does, the mechanism is unknown and the file blamed is the only thing the refusal names.
